scores.evidence: M1 thin slice → M2 usage/catalog → M3 lifecycle/corrections → M4 production readiness; T4 schema → T6 tenancy → T7 isolation suite → T8/T10/T13
scores.rationale: Milestones and tasks run substrate (infra, schema, RLS, tenancy) up to features with explicit dependencies and spikes proving unknowns before dependents.

scores.evidence: One thin slice deployed to staging through the real pipeline... flat monthly subscription... charged through a Stripe Connect test account, marked paid from Stripe's webhook
scores.rationale: M1 is a genuine end-to-end slice through CI/CD to staging before features; the only gap is that prod itself is gated to M4, which is acceptable.

scores.evidence: D2 ... Hard | Spike S1 shows >25% overhead or context leaks; or a tenant contractually needs a dedicated DB.
scores.rationale: Decision table lists options, reversibility, default and explicit revisit triggers, plus assumptions with impact and validation.

scores.evidence: T4 base schema and RLS lint → T6 tenancy middleware → T7 isolation suite before Catalog/Invoicing; scheduler fairness per environment
scores.rationale: Within M1 the widest-impact work (infra, schema, RLS, tenancy, ledger) precedes leaf features, and spikes of riskiest unknowns run early.

scores.evidence: Security (built in M1 unless noted)... cross-tenant suite on every PR; M2 hosted pages; M3 impersonation + audit UI; M4 pen test, QSA
scores.rationale: Security controls start in M1 (RLS, API key hashing, egress proxy, secrets, supply-chain scans) and recur in M2–M4 with concrete items.

scores.evidence: M1 builds the baseline and two alerts; the rest come with their components.
scores.rationale: Observability is in M1 (T16) but it comes after much of the build in task order, and later-phase treatment is thin (full alerts and runbooks mostly in M4).

scores.evidence: no console-created resources; staging applies from the pipeline only; Terraform, migrations as one-off ECS task, synthetic generators, test clocks
scores.rationale: IaC, pipeline-only deploys, migrations, deterministic test clocks and synthetic fixtures are threaded from M1 onward.

scores.evidence: Fault-injection tests: response dropped on create... duplicate webhook... circuit breaker; M2 load shedding; M3 dunning; M4 restore drill
scores.rationale: Failure handling (idempotency, forward-only state, reconcilers, backpressure, DLQ, restore drill) appears in each milestone starting M1.

scores.evidence: AI-specific concerns: not applicable. There are no model-driven components in scope.
scores.rationale: Plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Additional processors (Adyen, Braintree) | ≥2 qualified prospects blocked on them; the PaymentGateway port is the extension point
scores.rationale: Deferred table with explicit triggers, plus non-goals and intentional shortcuts with revisit conditions.

note: Very strong plan with walking skeleton, decision gates with flip conditions and explicit deferrals; only observability is slightly late and thin after M1.
